title: Nocturnal brain dump: Arthur Velasquez — runtime interview notes
content:
Context:
Role: Senior Runtime Engineer (inference stack) — loop with coding + system design + 30m behavioral.
Panel: Maya (lead), Diego (sre), me (shadow/notes).
Format: 90m total. Candidate arrived calm, grabbed whiteboard markers, asked clarifying questions early (good signal).

Quick one-liner impression:
Smart systems thinker, comfortable with latency SLO tradeoffs and cache mechanics, borderline on deliverable-ownership examples for this senior level. I lean toward a conditional pass with follow-up deep-dive. Confidence: 6/10.

Timeline / highlights (as I remember):
- 0-10m: intro + resume walk (focused on past infra projects at previous startup; emphasized shipping latency-critical features).
- 10-45m: design question: "Build a KV-cache layer for sharded LLM serving that keeps cold-start latencies < 40ms for 90th percentile".
- 45-75m: coding problem: small function to merge KV-cache metrics streams and compute eviction priorities given weighted recency + token-importance signals.
- 75-90m: behavioral + culture fit.

Design question notes (whiteboard):
Candidate structured answer: goals, constraints, metrics, core flow, failure modes. Very methodical.
Suggested architecture he sketched: local GPU-edge cache per shard + async background prefetch + central metadata store (etcd-like) for coordination. Used consistent hashing with virtual nodes to handle re-shards.
Good points:
- Recognized KV cache needs to be KV-by-prefix to support prefix reuse in autoregressive decoding.
- Called out cross-shard KV conflict when splitting context across GPUs and suggested read-replicas for hot prefixes.
- Prioritized latency SLOs over throughput for small requests; argued to serve from nearest replica instead of waiting for consensus.

Concerns / tradeoffs missed or glossed over:
- Not enough detail on cache coherence during model rollouts (how to invalidate stale kv across binary-compatible model versions). He mentioned "version tags" but didn't outline rollout coordination or migration steps.
- Prefetch logic: suggested heuristics (LRU-ish) but didn't quantify prefetch cost vs token budget. No concrete telemetry plan beyond "monitor miss_rate, p50/p90 latency".

Coding question (merged-streams + eviction priority):
- Candidate produced readable pseudocode; edge cases handled reasonably (empty streams, late-arriving metrics).
- Performance: algorithm was O(n log k) which is fine; he suggested a heap-based top-k eviction priority.
- Small bug: in the weighted recency calculation he normalized timestamps per-shard but forgot to account for clock skew in distributed metrics. I flagged but candidate acknowledged and proposed using monotonic counters or vector clocks. Good recovery.

Behavioral / ownership examples:
- Gave one strong example of owning a latency regression fix end-to-end: identified root cause (misconfigured batching), shipped a rolling config change, and added a canary to detect regressions. Good operational instincts.
- Weakness: when asked about mentoring and scaling a team, examples were surface-level (led 2 engineers) — not clear on cross-team influence expected at this level.

Scorecard (my subjective numbers):
- System design: 7/10 (clear architecture, missed rollout coherence details)
- Algorithms / coding: 7/10 (solid, minor bug, good recovery)
- Debugging / incident chops: 8/10 (credible example; pragmatic)
- Communication: 6/10 (structured but sometimes used jargon without grounding for non-runtime interviewers)
- Leadership / ownership: 5/10 (needs stronger cross-functional examples)
- Overall recommendation: conditional hire for Senior IC with pairing dive on rollout/coherence + mentorship examples.

Red flags (if any):
- Slight overreliance on heuristics without telemetry plan. Could lead to surprises in production if not instrumented.
- Not enough evidence of mentoring/leading across teams. For a senior hire we expect broader influence.

Suggested follow-ups / ask of candidate if moving forward:
- Ask for a 1-pager on rollout strategy for model + cache versioning: invalidation protocol, metrics to gate rollout, and rollback plan. Target: 1 page, 30 min read.
- Pair on a 60-90m design session specifically on KV coherence across sharded GPUs (we can include someone from serving runtime to probe kernel-level constraints).
- Request a short walk-through of a production incident they led with timelines, key decisions, and postmortem takeaways.

Hiring panel notes to record (practical):
- Compensation expectation: candidate said wide range; wants banding + clarity on career ladder.
- Start date: flexible, 4+ weeks.
- Work authorization: US-based, on EAD (mentioned briefly). Confirm with recruiting.

Action items (me / recruiting):
- [ ] Maya to share candidate's resume + coding exercise link with SRE interviewer for the second pass.
- [ ] Ask candidate for the 1-pager on rollout strategy before next interview.
- [ ] If recruiting wants to move forward, schedule the pairing session focused on cache coherence.

Loose thoughts (brain-dump):
- Might fit better as a "Senior II" where we emphasize technical depth but pair with a senior lead for org influence ramp.
- If they can demonstrate a crisp rollout doc and a mentoring story, they become a strong hire.
- Keep an eye on instrumentation bias: candidate tends to favor heuristics; pair with someone strong in observability.

Notes to self:
- Use their mention of "prefetch by n-gram importance" as a conversation starter with Maya — is that a pattern we want? Could be promising for Optimize product.
- Follow-up ticket: create small rubric for rollout/coherence that interviewers can use (3–4 checkboxes): invalidation plan, migration steps, metric gates, rollback threshold.

End of dump. TODO: tidy a short summary to post in Greenhouse before the panel sync.
